subject: StarFleet POC — resource alignment & success criteria
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Rao <asha@starfleet.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: StarFleet POC — resource alignment & success criteria

Hi Asha — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we spin up infra: 

Summary of call:
- Goal: validate StarFleet’s in-product summarization and chat flows using an in-domain 2-week POC.
- Success criteria (per your ask): 95% of summaries under 1.2x human baseline BLEU-ish proxy (your internal eval), end-to-end 200ms median generation latency for 512 token sequences at target concurrency, and cost target < $0.012/token (pre-quant).

What we propose for the POC (draft):
- Duration: 14 days of live testing (plus 3-day warm-up).
- Ownership: StarFleet product + data team to provide 500 example flows and scoring rubric; Redwood to provide serving, monitoring, and a configuration for autoscaling + caching.
- Evaluation plan: daily automated evals against your rubric, weekly quality review with human spot-checks, and a final pass/fail signoff based on thresholds above.

Capacity ask from StarFleet (action item): please confirm expected concurrent symptomatic users (QPS) and typical sequence length distribution (p50/p95 tokens). If you can attach a small sample of production-like payloads that will help us size properly.

Redwood baseline proposal (we can adjust once we get your numbers):
- Reserved capacity: 2 x A100 equivalent GPU nodes for baseline traffic (predictable latency).
- Autoscale policy: up to 6 additional GPUs for burst (scale increment = 2 GPUs, cooldown = 90s).
- Burst expectations: sustained bursts up to 2x baseline for 20–30 minutes; short bursts to 4x baseline for <5 minutes with queueing fallback.
- Prefetch/KV cache: enable per-session KV cache with a 6-hour cache window; this should reduce token-cost for multi-turn sessions.

Next steps:
1) Asha: send sample payloads + procurement contact for SOW.
2) Redwood: produce a proposed POC config (will attach redwood_poc_config.yaml) and a mutual action plan doc.
3) Align on go/no-go signoff criteria and schedule.

Attaching: mutual_action_plan.docx (draft), sample template for workload.

Thanks — I’ll hold on provisioning until we get the sample and confirmation of concurrency.

Best,
Rishi
VP Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: starfleet_mutual_action_plan.docx (Word), workload_template.csv (CSV)

From: Asha Rao <asha@starfleet.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Harris <ben.harris@starfleet.ai>, StarFleet Procurement <procurement@starfleet.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: StarFleet POC — resource alignment & success criteria

Thanks Rishi — this looks good. Quick answers / clarifications from our side: 

Load profile (expected):
- Peak concurrent requests (steady-state): ~120 QPS (typical user flows break into 2 calls each).
- Expected p50 length: 180 tokens; p95 length: 640 tokens (we have long context windows for a subset of flows).
- Typical concurrency shape: predictable daily peak (US PST lunch) and occasional campaigns where traffic spikes ~3x for ~10–40 minutes.

Evaluation details:
- We will provide a dataset of ~800 labeled flows and a small human evaluation pool to spot-check 50 samples/day. Our internal rubric is attached (starfleet_poc_workload_sample.csv).

Procurement: please route SOW and a 14-day trial agreement to procurement@starfleet.ai — Ben Harris is the POC for procurement.

One question on autoscale: for short high spikes (10–40 minutes) we want a soft cap that avoids cold-start latencies but still limits cost. Can Redwood guarantee a warm pool or pre-warm hooks? If so, what latency should we expect when bursting to 4x baseline?

We can confirm the dataset by EOD tomorrow. Once you send the proposed config we’ll get procurement moving.

—Asha
Director, Product @ StarFleet AI

Attachment: starfleet_poc_workload_sample.csv (CSV, 800 rows)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Rao <asha@starfleet.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Ben Harris <ben.harris@starfleet.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: StarFleet POC — resource alignment & success criteria

Asha — thanks for the fast turnaround and the payload sample. Based on your p95 = 640 tokens and 120 QPS steady-state, here’s a concrete config we recommend for the POC (attached as redwood_poc_config.yaml):

Concrete capacity recommendation (POC):
- Baseline reserved: 3 x A100-equivalent GPUs (we increased from 2 after seeing p95 and concurrency to keep median latency <=200ms for 512-tokens and p95 <=450ms for 640 tokens).
- Warm pool: 2 warmed GPU instances held in a warm pool for immediate burst (these count as partly reserved — billed at a reduced pre-warm rate).
- Autoscale ceiling: scale to a max of 8 GPUs for extreme bursts. Scaling steps: +2 GPUs at a time, scale cooldown 90s, pre-warm hook to allocate warmed instances when we see signals from your traffic router.
- Queue fallback: when ceiling hit, requests will be queued for up to 8s with a progressive degrade mode that returns shorter summaries for timeouts.
- Caching: per-session KV cache + request-level response cache for identical prompts (TTL 6 hours).

Latency expectations when bursting to 4x baseline with warm pool enabled:
- Cold-start (no warm pre-warm): first new GPU ~18–28s to be ready; median token latency elevated for first 30–60s.
- Warm pool present: new requests routed to warm pool instances with <700ms additional cold-penalty; median generation still within 1.3x of baseline for most sequences.

Cost/contract note: pre-warmed instances incur a partial reservation charge; we’ll show cost delta in the SOW. For a 14-day POC we can offer a trial pricing line item (will include in SOW).

Action items:
- Rishi: attach redwood_poc_config.yaml and a draft MOU/SOW for procurement (DocuSign link).
- Asha: confirm you’re ok with baseline = 3 GPUs + 2 warm pool, and authorize procurement contact.
- David: please review the config and confirm the autoscale cooldown and queueing approach below.

Attaching: redwood_poc_config.yaml (POC config), draft_SOW_link (DocuSign placeholder).

Thanks — aiming to sign and provision next week if Procurement moves quickly.

Best,
Rishi
VP Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: redwood_poc_config.yaml (YAML), draft_SOW_link (DocuSign)

From: David Kim <david@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Asha Rao <asha@starfleet.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 24 Oct 2026 14:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: StarFleet POC — resource alignment & success criteria

Looping in a few infra/ops notes from our side — thanks for the numbers, Asha. Two clarifying items we need so sizing is precise: 

1) Concurrency model: are the 120 QPS expressed as single-token streaming requests or as full-generation calls? For streaming we treat token throughput differently.
2) Sequence composition: how often does the model run with context > 2k tokens (we quoted p95=640 but corner cases matter for KV storage).

Operational notes: 
- Warm pool mechanics: we can keep 2 instances pre-warmed but they will cycle every 6 hours to avoid memory fragmentation; there will be brief handover windows (~150–400ms) while routing updates.
- Autoscale signal: best trigger is a mix of 95th-percentile CPU/GPU utilization + request queue depth; we recommend we instrument a 30s moving average to avoid oscillation.
- Logging/observability: we will emit token-level latency and per-route cost estimates; we will also provide a daily digest to your team.

David — can you confirm whether the queue TTL = 8s is acceptable? We need to make sure UX for your product tolerates progressive degradation.

If StarFleet can provide one example of a 2k+ token flow, we’ll include a stress test run in our baseline.

—David
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Asha Rao <asha@starfleet.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Harris <ben.harris@starfleet.ai>, StarFleet Procurement <procurement@starfleet.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: StarFleet POC — resource alignment & success criteria

Thanks everyone — this is clear and reasonable. Quick answers: 
- 120 QPS = full-generation calls (not streaming) with 2 calls per user flow on average. We have ~6% of flows that spike >2k tokens; attaching one anonymized 2.3k-token example for your stress test.
- Queue TTL = 8s is acceptable; prefer queue + degrade to returning a short summary rather than outright failures.

Procurement note: Ben will spin up the SOW review today and expects to sign a 14-day trial SOW if the DocuSign is received. Ben (copied) — please confirm procurement timeline.

We accept the baseline as proposed (3 reserved GPUs + 2 warm pool + autoscale to 8). Please send the DocuSign link and we’ll route internally. Looking forward to the stress test results and kickoff timeline.

Regards,
Asha Rao
Director, Product @ StarFleet AI

Attachment: long_example_2300tokens.json (anonymized)
